articles.title: EXPLORE DRUPAL VIA ACQUIA'S TRIAL
HUMANS APPROVE INTENT, MACHINES PROVE CONFORMANCE
articles.summary: Gittifacts routes agent-written changes to auto-merge, quick review, or full review based on test evidence and repository policy, after a human approves the plan. Missing signals can only increase scrutiny, and feature flags make merged changes reversible. Auto-merge still relies on the submitting agent's test environment for some evidence, while evidence generation took 13 to 17 minutes per change on the project's own repository.

articles.title: EXPLORING AWS LAMBDA WEB FUNCTIONS FOR BUILDING WEB APPLICATIONS
articles.summary: AWS Lambda Web Functions run standard Node.js HTTP servers without adapters, with each execution environment handling concurrent requests and streaming responses. In a sample run of 300 streaming requests with up to 200 open at once, five environments consumed 4.75 seconds of CPU. Billing covers active CPU, memory, and requests, so waiting on a database or API uses little CPU but still incurs other charges.

articles.title: HYBRIDAGENT THINKS IN LATENT SPACE AND ACTS IN TEXT
articles.summary: HybridAgent is a research approach for training AI agents to reason internally using numerical representations instead of writing out every intermediate thought, while still producing text to call tools such as Python or web search and deliver answers. In tests, a 14B Qwen3 model trained this way scored 52.4 on GAIA versus 43.7 for a matched text-only agent, with estimated decoding costs falling from $470 to $176 per million questions.

articles.title: SOMEONE BEHIND THE SOFTWARE
articles.summary: Good products reflect a shared point of view shaped by experience, customer conversations, and judgment. When teams use agents to add features independently, individually useful changes can weaken the product's coherence unless someone keeps shaping the whole.

articles.title: WHAT REQUIREMENTS DON'T YOU HAVE?
articles.summary: Elegant systems often gain simplicity and scale by accepting limits on freshness, coordination, or flexibility. Coding agents tend to invent extra requirements, so explicitly stating which compromises are acceptable can prevent unnecessary locks, checks, and layers of abstraction.

articles.title: DOES RUBY ON RAILS STILL MAKE SENSE?
articles.summary: Frameworks remain useful when agents write the code because they supply structure, shared maintenance, and familiar abstractions. Rewriting an application in a faster language can change behavior that users rely on, making targeted optimization and dependency updates a more practical starting point. Familiar code also makes it easier to review the decisions an agent makes.

articles.title: WEBINAR: WHAT AI AGENTS COST YOU WHEN THEY DON'T UNDERSTAND YOUR BUSINESS
articles.summary: When AI agents fall short, it's rarely the model. An agent that can't resolve something keeps exploring, and you pay for it to rediscover what the business already knows. In this webinar, we'll cover what context failure actually costs, in tokens, time and output quality. Save your spot [12].

articles.title: DEEPSEEK SEARCH & FETCH
articles.summary: DeepSeek's Search and Fetch APIs give agents and RAG applications live search results and web pages converted to Markdown. Both use standard DeepSeek API keys and cost $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests, with empty results, failures, and timeouts excluded from billing.

articles.title: SPHINX
articles.summary: Sphinx pauses pushes to protected branches and quizzes developers on what agent-written code does, including failure scenarios. A separate reviewer reads the diff without seeing the development chat, explains incorrect answers, and asks a new scenario before allowing the push. It supports existing coding agents and configurable model endpoints, with a logged bypass for skipped checks.

articles.title: RAKAZO
articles.summary: Rakazo is an open-source, self-hosted AI assistant for running persistent bots with their own memory, routines, and conversations. Bots can use browsers, terminals, files, and desktop interfaces, with your choice of model and local or hosted computer environments. The project is in beta and offers web, desktop, and mobile clients.

articles.title: SENIOR SOFTWARE ENGINEER, APPLIED AI AT TLDR ($300K BASE + $60K BONUS, FULLY REMOTE)
articles.summary: TLDR is hiring a senior engineer to build the agent-first operating layer used across the company. We're looking for a builder who has taken an LLM agent to production and still owns it. Click here to learn more [17].

articles.title: NEW TREND OF BUILDING "INTERNAL VIBE-CODING APPS" AT TECH COMPANIES
articles.summary: Ramp and Stripe built internal AI coding platforms that let non-engineers create tools using company data and design systems. Stripe's Harbor was built by one engineer in around six weeks, while creating a tool in Ramp's Glass is now part of new-hire onboarding. The appeal includes easier access to internal data, fewer vendor negotiations, and hands-on experience building AI infrastructure.

articles.title: GEMINI 4 ARGON VS. CLAUDE OPUS 5.5
articles.summary: In a comparison run once per model, Gemini 4 Argon matched Claude Opus 5.5 on finding and fixing 14 planted bugs at lower cost, but performed worse on billing and long-context dependency tasks. One incorrect API call caused most billing failures, and a manual one-line fix brought Argon to full marks. Its long-context answers still missed or invented dependencies, showing why the results need to be read beyond the headline scores.

articles.title: CLAUDE REVEALS ECDSA CURVE ORIGINS
articles.summary: An internal Claude research model traced the seeds of five NIST prime curves to the lrand48 random-number generator initialized with Unix timestamps, explaining a decades-old provenance mystery. Anthropic says the findings strengthen confidence in the curves and do not reveal a cryptographic break. Some base-point origins, skipped candidates, and one binary-curve seed remain unexplained.

articles.title: WHAT THE HECK IS /PKG?
articles.summary: macOS 27 adds /pkg/env/global/bin to PATH, but the directory's purpose remains unexplained, and a possible Apple package manager is still speculation.

articles.title: LLM INFERENCE ON THE APPLE NEURAL ENGINE
articles.summary: MacPaw's tests of LFM2.5-2.6B across three Macs found Neural Engine inference used 2.6 to 3.4 times less energy than MLX 8-bit with speculative decoding on typical requests, while long contexts benefited from splitting work with the GPU.

articles.title: IF YOU DON'T RUN YOUR OWN LLM PROXY, HOW THE FUCK DO YOU EVEN KNOW WHAT'S GOING ON?
articles.summary: A self-hosted LLM proxy gives developers detailed usage logs, virtual API keys, and a single endpoint for multiple models and providers, making it easier to investigate cache misses and switch services.
